text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Severity 2 — multiple TLS handshake failures impacting hosted-api in us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-15T02:10Z. Symptoms: increased 5xx and 524s, early TLS termination in client traces. Paging oncall: @Maya, @Raj. Runbook: <https://runbook.internal/incidents/tls-handshake|TLS handshake runbook>

Maya: Oncall Maya here — I'm looking at ingress logs and gateway traces now. Can someone post the first failing curl/openssl output?

Eva: pasting curl from ci smoke: 
```
$ curl -v https://api-hosted.us-west-2.redwood.internal/health
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api-hosted.us-west-2.redwood.internal (10.1.5.22) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* read:errno=104
* Connection reset by peer
curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
```

Raj: Thanks. That looks like premature connection reset during handshake. Did we rotate TLS certs overnight? deploy-bot, did any cert-related rollout run in the last 12h?

deploy-bot: automated-deploy: cert-rotation job started 2026-03-15T00:45Z -> completed 2026-03-15T01:05Z (applied to hosted-api-us-west-2) :white_check_mark:

Maya: OK, cert rotation happened. Hypothesis list (initial):
- H1: bad certs (wrong SAN, missing intermediate, key mismatch)
- H2: broken TLS termination at gateway (conn reset from sidecar/proxy)
- H3: networking fragmentation/MTU causing TLS records to drop -> handshake aborts
- H4: VPC peering route flap causing asymmetric path -> middlebox reset

Ken: I spun tcpdump on the gateway egress. Seeing a lot of `ICMP frag needed` + MSS negotiation from upstream around 02:08-02:12Z. Snippet: 
```
02:09:11.123456 IP host-gw > peer-gw: ICMP Frag needed, mtu 1400, length 1500
02:09:11.123458 IP client > host-gw: 443 TLS Client Hello
02:09:11.123465 IP host-gw > client: RST
```

Maya: That's interesting — ICMP fragmentation needed suggests MTU mismatch on the peering link. If TLS ClientHello gets fragmented and middlebox drops fragments we could see handshake fail.

Alice (support): Customer impact: Support telemetry shows a spike in TLS failures for 3 enterprise customers (org-23, org-77, org-108) in us-west-2. Estimated failed requests ~3.2k in last hour, error rate peaking at 18% for those tenants. Noted some timeouts from CloudFront frontends -> backend. No data loss reported.

Raj: I'm checking Vault audit logs for cert rotation details. Found rotation event: 
```
2026-03-15T00:48:56Z vault.audit: user=ci-cd service=cert-rotator action=rotate_cert cluster=hosted-api-us-west-2 cert_id=crt-20260315-01
metadata: old_serial=0x7f4... new_serial=0x9a2..., san=[api-hosted.us-west-2.redwood.internal, hosted-api.redwood.internal]
```

Maya: The SANs look correct. So H1 is lower probability. Also we deployed rotation at 01:05Z but errors spike at ~02:10Z — gap suggests something else changed or network path degraded.

Ken: I also pulled VPC flow logs for the peering connection. Saw intermittent ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) and some SYN retransmits. Flow log snippet: 
```
src=10.1.5.22 dst=10.200.3.11 proto=6 action=REJECT reason=FragmentationNeeded
```

Maya: Can someone run an `openssl s_client -connect` from edge node to backend and capture TCP-MSS behavior?

Ken: Running now: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.200.3.11:443 -tls1_2 -msg
CONNECTED(00000003)
>>> TLS 1.2 Handshake, ClientHello
<<< read from 0x7f9a8a0: Connection reset by peer
139771234567808:error:140:SSL routines:CONNECT_CR_SRVR_HELLO:SSL3_GET_SERVER_HELLO:ssl_lib.c:212
```

Ken: Also ran `ping -M do -s 1472` (to test for 1500 MTU) and got `Frag needed` responses. Lowering to 1400 works.

Maya: That points to MTU mismatch on the path. H3 gains weight. Still need to rule out TLS termination config. Can someone snapshot proxy logs for TLS handshake failures (nginx/envoy)?

Raj: Envoy stats show `downstream_cx_connect_fail` and `tls_handshake_failure` spikes at 02:10Z. No obvious config reloads at that time.

Eva: I rolled back to previous cert version as a quick test (ensured cert matches previous serial). Re-deployed to a canary instance -> still failing for canary. So cert rollback didn't fix it.

Maya: Confirmed: cert rollback no impact => deprioritize H1. Moving forward with network remediation. Action: apply MSS clamp on NAT gateways and update peering MTU setting if possible. Raj, can you coordinate with cloud infra to enable MSS clamping at edge?

Raj: Request submitted to cloud infra runbook, also opened a ticket with cloud provider for peering MTU (case #CP-4629). Applying a temporary iptables clamp on the gateway nodes now: 
```
sudo iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
Applying on host-gw-*. Took effect at ~02:36Z.

Ken: After MSS clamp, tcpdump shows MSS reduced to 1360 on SYN, and TLS handshakes start succeeding. Sample logs: 
```
02:37:02.234 IP client > host-gw: SYN MSS=1360
02:37:02.240 IP host-gw > peer-gw: SYN MSS=1360
02:37:02.412 TLS handshake completed
```

Alice (support): Error rate for affected tenants dropped from 18% -> 1.2% within 10 minutes of fix. No further customer escalations.

Maya: Excellent. Current status: traffic recovered to baseline by 02:50Z. Root cause likely: peering path MTU mismatch (probably introduced by a change in transit network or intermediate appliance) causing fragmentation of TLS records and handshake failures. The cert rotation earlier was a red herring.

Raj: Timeline summary to include in RCA: 
- 00:45–01:05Z: automated cert rotation applied (no immediate failures)
- 02:08–02:12Z: first TLS handshake failures and ICMP Frag needed observed
- 02:10Z: paging triggered (this thread)
- 02:20–02:35Z: collection of tcpdump, flow logs, Vault audit, Envoy stats; hypotheses triaged
- 02:36Z: iptables MSS clamp applied on gateway nodes (temporary mitigation)
- 02:50Z: traffic recovered to baseline

Ken: Artifacts collected and attached to incident packet: tcpdump (pcap), VPC flow logs, envoys/stats snapshots, vault audit export. Location: <https://internal-artifacts/incidents/1849004567>

Maya: Post-incident action items (ownership):
- (Infra) Ensure peering MTU validation added to network canary and alert on ICMP Frag needed logs. (owner: Ken)
- (Platform) Add TLS handshake failure rate alert tied to unusual `ICMP frag` spike. (owner: Maya)
- (Platform) Update cert-rotation runbook to include immediate connectivity smoke tests post-rotation. (owner: Raj)
- (SRE) Replace temporary iptables clamp with long-term fix: coordinate with cloud provider to fix peering MTU or change transit appliance config. (owner: Raj + Infra)
- (Support) Customer follow-ups: notify affected orgs with timeline and mitigation steps. (owner: Alice)

Alice (support): I'll prepare customer-facing note and send to CSMs.

Maya: Handoff: I'm closing active paging. Raj you own the follow-up RCA and cloud provider case. I'll take incident writeup and run the postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 PST.

Raj: Ack. I'll escalate peering MTU with provider and attach provider response to RCA.

incident-bot: Incident stabilized — status: mitigated. Severity updated to SEV-2 -> follow-up RCA scheduled.

Maya: Adding final note: check internal monitoring for any residual TLS handshake anomalies and ensure canary traffic includes large ClientHello sizes to exercise fragmentation edge cases.

-- end of thread --
